(5) Node
      22.23.4 on a bare node:http server (not project code): 1 000 header lines in all → 200, 1 001 → 431, 2 500 short
      lines `a:b` (12 536 bytes) → 431, a normal request after them → 200; with `maxHeadersCount = 0` the 2 500 lines →

      probe of the count keeps the head under 16 384 bytes.
edits.became:
(5) Node
      22.23.4 on a bare node:http server (not project code): the count limit is 1 000 header lines in all (Host
      included): 1 000 → 200, 1 001 → 431, 2 500 short lines `a:b` (12 536 bytes) → 431, a normal request after them →
      200; with `maxHeadersCount = 0` the 2 500 lines → 200. The 16 KiB size limit counts the bytes of the header
      names and values, not the whole head: 500 lines in all with names and values of 16 344 bytes (a head of 18 362)
      → 200, of 16 842 bytes (a head of 18 860) → 431; 990 lines with 15 718 bytes (a head of 19 696) → 200; 300 lines
      with 60-byte values, 18 982 bytes → 431 (measured at step 2c; the gate measured the same on the clone's Pixel
      Office server, step 2b, F4). So a head under 16 384 bytes is a sufficient bound for a probe of the count.
